verdict.rationale: GitCafe's official CLI documents non-interactive automation flags: `--json` for structured output, `--no-input` to fail instead of prompting, and `--yes` to confirm destructive actions. Personal access tokens are explicitly meant for scripts and CI jobs using the REST API or Git over HTTPS, and `cafe api` gives scriptable authenticated API access. missing for 10: explicit documentation of authenticating the CLI headlessly in CI (e.g. a token env var instead of the browser-based `cafe auth login`), independent or hands-on corroboration of CI usage.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can run the product headlessly / in CI for automation

citations.quote: `--json` prints structured output; progress and errors go to stderr. `--no-input` fails instead of prompting; `--yes` confirms destructive actions.
A personal access token lets scripts, CI jobs and tools use the REST API or Git over HTTPS as you, with only the permissions you grant.
`cafe api <path>` sends an authenticated request to any REST API endpoint.
